Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Interface RuleListener

All Known Implementing Classes:
LoggingRuleListener
public interface RuleListener
A listener interface to hook into the lifecycle of rule evaluation and execution. Implement this interface to receive callbacks before and after rules are evaluated and executed. Any exception thrown by a listener, including a StackOverflowError, an AssertionError or a LinkageError such as NoClassDefFoundError, is caught and logged by the engine, ensuring the core execution is not interrupted. A VirtualMachineError such as an OutOfMemoryError propagates out of run() once every listener has received the same callback, also when it is the cause of an exception the listener throws. If it came from a before* callback, the condition or action doesn't run, and every listener first gets onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException) to close that callback. When onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException) closes a failure that is fatal itself, whether the rule or a before* callback threw that error, and a listener throws another VirtualMachineError there, the failure's own error is still the one run() throws: the first such error, other than that failure's own, is suppressed on the exception onRunError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext, java.lang.RuntimeException) gets, and any later one is only logged.

Thread safety: an engine shared across threads invokes the same listener from every thread calling run(), possibly at the same time, so implementations must be thread-safe. Listeners are added when the engine is built, with RulesEngineBuilder.listener(RuleListener), and can't change afterwards.

A Rule is immutable, so every callback receives the rule as it was passed to RulesEngine.load(java.util.List): the same instance each time.

Implementing: every callback has a default that does nothing, so override only the ones you need. A callback added in a later 2.x release also has a default that does nothing, so an existing listener keeps compiling and working.

  • Method Details

    • beforeRun

      default void beforeRun(RunContext run)
      Called when a run starts, before any condition is evaluated. It's followed by exactly one call to afterRun(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunResult<?>) or onRunError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext, java.lang.RuntimeException), so a span, timer or logging context opened here can always be closed.

      A run that waits for a compiled copy of the rules opens its scope when the wait ends, so the wait isn't inside the pair. A run() that fails because no rules are loaded, or because the engine is closed, is misuse and reaches no callback. One that fails because the engine's rule list was closed over and over while it was borrowing a copy reaches none either: that means an engine invariant has broken rather than that the call was wrong.

      Parameters:
      run - The run, which identifies it and carries its facts, the checksum of the rules it uses, and the tags and start time that choose which of them it uses

    • afterRun

      default void afterRun(RunContext run, RunResult<?> result)
      Called when a run has finished, after the last after* callback.
      Parameters:
      run - The run that beforeRun(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext) opened
      result - What the run did: the output object, the rules that fired, each rule's outcome, the rules' checksum, and the run's tags and start time

    • onRunError

      default void onRunError(RunContext run, RuntimeException error)
      Called when a run fails, in place of afterRun(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunResult<?>). Unlike onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException), this reports the failures that belong to no rule too, such as a stopped run or an output supplier that throws. A failure inside a rule reaches that rule's onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException) first, then this callback. A run that fails before it starts, because a language throws or returns null when it creates a session for the run, reaches no listener at all.

      error is what run() throws. When run() rethrows a fatal Error instead, error is a RuleExecutionException that carries it. If the error came while a rule's callback was open, from the rule, a listener's before* callback or a listener's onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException), that is the exception onError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.exception.RuleExecutionException) got, which names the rule unless the run was stopped; for one from anywhere else, such as a listener's beforeRun(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext), afterEvaluate(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, boolean) or afterExecute(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, java.lang.Object), it names no rule.

      Parameters:
      run - The run that beforeRun(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext) opened
      error - The failure; run() throws it, or the fatal Error it wraps

    • onError

      default void onError(Rule rule, RuleExecutionException error)
      Called when evaluating a rule's condition or executing its action fails, in place of afterEvaluate(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>, boolean) or afterExecute(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.Rule, java.lang.Object). Every before* callback is followed by exactly one call to the matching after* method or to this method.

      error is the exception that run() throws once all listeners have been notified. An Error the condition or action throws is wrapped in it; for a fatal VirtualMachineError such as an OutOfMemoryError, error wraps it and run() rethrows the original error instead. Errors found while compiling rules in load() are not reported here.

      A run stopped between rules, because its thread was interrupted or it passed its deadline, is not reported here, because no callback for the next rule is open: only onRunError(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RunContext, java.lang.RuntimeException) is called. A run stopped while a condition or action was running, which returns or throws once the run is cancelled, closes that rule's callback here: error then has no rule name and an InterruptedException or a TimeoutException as its cause. That holds unless what it threw has an Error anywhere in its cause chain: that rule's own failure is reported instead, exactly as it would be with no stop pending, so error names the rule and has what the expression threw as its cause.

      Parameters:
      rule - The rule whose condition or action failed
      error - The failure; run() throws it, or the fatal Error it wraps
